title.zh: 卷四六 補列傳第三八 循吏
title.raw: 卷四六 補列傳第三八 循吏 Volume 46 Biographies 38: Good Officials

sentences.zh: 張華原 宋世良 弟世軌 郎基 孟業 崔伯謙 蘇瓊 房豹 路去病

translations.literal: Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, younger brother Shigui, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, Lu Qubing
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, his younger brother Shigui, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing

sentences.zh: 先王疆理天下，司牧黎元，刑法以禁其奸，禮教以防其欲。

translations.literal: The former kings divided and ordered the realm, shepherded the black-haired people, used penal law to forbid their wickedness, and used ritual teaching to guard against their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings divided the realm and tended the people, using penal law to forbid wickedness and ritual teaching to guard against desire.

sentences.zh: 故分職命官，共理天下。

translations.literal: Therefore offices were divided and officials appointed to govern the realm together.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they divided offices and appointed officials to govern the realm together.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「知人則哲，能官人安人則惠。

translations.literal: The Book says: "To know men is to be wise; to be able to place men in office and settle men is to be gracious.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "To know men is wisdom; to place men in office and settle the people is grace.

sentences.zh: 」睿哲之君，必致清明之臣，昏亂之朝，多有貪殘之吏。

translations.literal: " A wise and perspicacious lord is sure to obtain clear and bright ministers; a benighted and chaotic court has many greedy and cruel clerks.
translations.idiomatic: " A wise ruler wins clear-minded ministers; a benighted court breeds greedy, cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 高祖撥亂反正，恤隱為懷，故守令之徒，才多稱職。

translations.literal: Gao Huan set right the disorder and turned back to the proper, with pity for the hidden in his breast, so among prefects and magistrates many were fit for their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan set the realm right after chaos and held pity close, so many prefects and magistrates proved fit for their posts.

sentences.zh: 仍以戰功諸將，出牧外藩，不識治體，無聞政術。

translations.literal: Yet he still sent generals of battle merit out to pasture the outer marches; they did not know the substance of governance and had not heard of the arts of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still sent battle-hardened generals to govern the outer marches—men who knew nothing of governance and had never learned the arts of rule.

sentences.zh: 非唯暗於前言往行，乃至始學依判付曹，聚斂無厭，淫虐不已，雖或直繩，終無悛革。

translations.literal: Not only were they dark to words and deeds of old, they even began by learning to hand cases to clerks by precedent; insatiable in exaction, unceasing in debauchery and cruelty—though sometimes the straight cord was applied, in the end there was no repentance or reform.
translations.idiomatic: They were blind not only to precedent but even began by learning to hand cases to clerks by template; insatiable in levies, relentless in cruelty—though the law was sometimes enforced, they never truly reformed.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 此朝廷之大失。

translations.literal: This was a great loss of the court.
translations.idiomatic: This was a grave loss for the court.

sentences.zh: 大寧以後，風雅俱缺，賣官鬻獄，上下相蒙，降及末年，黷貨滋甚。

translations.literal: After Daining, elegance and refinement were both lacking; offices and prisons were sold, above and below deceived one another, and down to the final years venal goods grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daining era, refinement vanished; offices and judgments were sold, court and country deceived one another, and in the dynasty's last years venality grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 齊氏循良，如辛術之徒非一，多以官爵通顯，別有列傳。

translations.literal: Among Qi there were good officials such as Xin Shu—not one alone—many of whom rose to prominence through rank and title and have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi had good officials—Xin Shu was not alone—many of whom won rank and fame and have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 如房仲幹之屬，在武平之末能，卓爾不群，斯固彌可嘉也。

translations.literal: Men such as Fang Zhonggan, able at the end of Wuping to stand out from the crowd, are all the more worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Fang Zhonggan, who at the end of Wuping still stood apart from the crowd, are all the more praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 今掇張華原等列於《循吏》云。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Huayuan and the rest are gathered and listed in Good Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Here Zhang Huayuan and the rest are gathered under Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 張華原，字國滿，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Huayuan, style Guoman, was a man of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huayuan, style Guoman, was from Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少明敏，有器度。

translations.literal: In youth he was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bright and keen, with real capacity.

sentences.zh: 高祖開驃騎府，引為法曹參軍，遷大丞相府屬，仍侍左右。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan opened the Rapid Cavalry Office he brought him in as legal-cases staff officer, promoted him to staff of the Grand Chancellor's office, and still attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan opened the Rapid Cavalry Office he made Huayuan a legal-cases staff officer, then a staff member of the Grand Chancellor's office, still attending at his side.

sentences.zh: 從於信都，深為高祖所親待。

translations.literal: He followed him to Xindu and was deeply favored and treated by Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan to Xindu and was deeply favored.

sentences.zh: 高祖每號令三軍，常令宣諭意旨。

translations.literal: Whenever Gao Huan issued orders to the three armies he often had Huayuan proclaim and explain his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gao Huan commanded the three armies he often had Huayuan proclaim his intent.

sentences.zh: 周文帝始據雍州也，高祖猶欲以逆順曉之，使華原入關說焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first held Yong province, Gao Huan still wished to enlighten him with right and wrong and sent Huayuan into the passes to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first held Yong province, Gao Huan still hoped to persuade him with the logic of loyalty and rebellion and sent Huayuan through the passes to argue with him.

sentences.zh: 周文密有拘留之意，謂華原曰：「若能屈驥足於此，當共享富貴，不爾，命懸今日。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen secretly intended detention and said to Huayuan: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs here, we shall share wealth and honor together; if not, your life hangs on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen secretly meant to detain him and said: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs to stay here, we shall share wealth and honor; if not, your life ends today.

sentences.zh: 」華原曰：「渤海王命世誕生，殆天所縱，以明公蕞爾關右，便自隔絕，故使華原銜喻公旨。

translations.literal: " Huayuan said: "The Prince of Bohai was born to order the age—perhaps Heaven set him free. With your lordship's petty hold on the western passes you have cut yourselves off, so Huayuan was sent to carry your lordship's message.
translations.idiomatic: " Huayuan said: "The Prince of Bohai was born to order the age—perhaps Heaven itself set him free. Your lordship holds only the western passes and has cut yourselves off; Huayuan was sent to carry your message.

sentences.zh: 明公不以此日改圖，轉禍為福，乃欲賜脅，有死而已。

translations.literal: If your lordship will not on this day change your plan and turn calamity into blessing, yet wish to bestow coercion, there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not change course today and turn calamity into blessing, but mean to coerce me, there is only death.

sentences.zh: 」周文嘉其亮正，乃使東還。

translations.literal: " Zhou Wen admired his candor and uprightness and sent him back east.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Wen admired his candor and sent him back east.

sentences.zh: 高祖以華原久而不返，每嘆惜之，及聞其來，喜見於色。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, because Huayuan had long not returned, often sighed in regret; when he heard he had come, joy showed in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had long sighed over Huayuan's absence; when he heard of his return, joy showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 累遷為兗州刺史，人懷感附，寇盜寢息。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became inspector of Yan province; the people were moved and attached themselves, and bandits and robbers lay quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in time to inspector of Yan, he won the people's attachment and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 州獄先有囚千餘人，華原皆決遣。

translations.literal: The provincial prison had formerly held more than a thousand prisoners; Huayuan decided and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial prison had held more than a thousand prisoners; Huayuan judged and released them all.

sentences.zh: 至年暮，唯有重罪者數十人，華原亦遣歸家申賀，依期至獄。

translations.literal: At year's end only several dozen men of heavy crime remained; Huayuan also sent them home to offer New Year's congratulations, to return to prison on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end only several dozen men of serious crime remained; Huayuan sent even them home for New Year's greetings, on promise to return to prison on schedule.

sentences.zh: 先是州境數有猛獸為暴，自華原臨州，忽有六駁食之，咸以化感所致。

translations.literal: Before this, within the province fierce beasts had often ravaged; from the time Huayuan took the province, suddenly six piebald horses devoured them— all took it as the effect of transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: Before, fierce beasts had often ravaged the province; once Huayuan took office, six piebald horses suddenly devoured them—all called it the fruit of his transforming influence.

sentences.zh: 後卒官，州人大小莫不號慕。

translations.literal: Later he died in office; great and small among the people all cried out in longing.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office; people great and small mourned him aloud.

sentences.zh: 宋世良，字元友，廣平人。

translations.literal: Song Shiliang, style Yuanyou, was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shiliang, style Yuanyou, was from Guangping.

sentences.zh: 年十五便有膽氣，應募從軍北討，屢有戰功。

translations.literal: At fifteen he already had daring spirit; he answered the call and followed the army on the northern campaign, repeatedly winning battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he already had daring; he enlisted for the northern campaign and won battle merit again and again.

sentences.zh: 尋為殿中侍御史，詣河北括戶，大獲浮惰。

translations.literal: Soon he became attendant censor of the palace and went to Hebei to register households, greatly uncovering hidden and idle persons.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became palace attendant censor and went to Hebei to register households, uncovering many hidden and idle persons.

sentences.zh: 還見汲郡城旁多骸骨，移書州郡，令悉收瘞。

translations.literal: On his return he saw many bones beside Jiyin city and sent letters to the provinces and commanderies ordering all collected and buried.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he saw many bones beside Jiyin city and wrote the provinces and commanderies to collect and bury them all.

sentences.zh: 其夜，甘雨霶沱。

translations.literal: That night sweet rain poured in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: That night sweet rain poured down.

sentences.zh: 還，孝莊勞之曰：「知卿所括得丁倍於本帳，若官人皆如此用心，便是更出一天下也。」

translations.literal: On his return, Emperor Xiaozhuang rewarded him, saying: "I know the households you registered doubled the original rolls; if every official were so intent, it would be like bringing forth another realm under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Back at court, Emperor Xiaozhuang praised him: "The households you registered doubled the original rolls; if every official worked like you, it would be as if another realm had appeared under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 出除清河太守。

translations.literal: He went out and was removed to be prefect of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世良才識閑明，尤善治術，在郡未幾，聲問甚高。

translations.literal: Shiliang's talent and insight were clear and bright, especially skilled in the arts of rule; within the commandery, before long, his reputation was very high.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was clear and bright in talent, especially skilled in governance; within the commandery his fame rose quickly.

sentences.zh: 郡東南有曲堤，成公一姓阻而居之，群盜多萃於此。

translations.literal: Southeast of the commandery was the Crooked Dike, where the Cheng clan alone blocked and dwelt and many bandits gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the commandery lay Crooked Dike, where the Cheng clan alone held the ground and bandits gathered thickly.

sentences.zh: 人為之語曰：「寧度東吳會稽，不歷成公曲堤。

translations.literal: Men made a saying of it: "Better cross the Wu region and Kuaiji than pass Cheng's Crooked Dike.
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Better cross Wu and Kuaiji than pass Cheng's Crooked Dike.

sentences.zh: 」世良施八條之制，盜奔他境。

translations.literal: " Shiliang applied the eight-article system and the bandits fled to other districts.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiliang applied his eight-article system and the bandits fled to other districts.

sentences.zh: 民又謠曰：「曲堤雖險賊何益，但有宋公自屏跡。

translations.literal: The people again made a rhyme: "Though Crooked Dike is steep, what good are the bandits?—so long as Lord Song screens their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: The people rhymed: "Though Crooked Dike is steep, what good are bandits?—Lord Song alone screens their tracks.

sentences.zh: 」後齊天保中大赦，郡先無一囚，羣吏拜詔而已。

translations.literal: " Later in the Tianbao era's great amnesty, the commandery had not a single prisoner beforehand; the clerks merely bowed to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, at Tianbao's great amnesty, the commandery had not one prisoner beforehand—the clerks only bowed to the edict.

sentences.zh: 獄內穞生，桃樹、蓬蒿亦滿。

translations.literal: Inside the prison millet grew, and peach trees and artemisia filled it too.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the prison millet grew, and peach trees and artemisia filled the yards.

sentences.zh: 每日衙門虛寂，無復訴訟者。

translations.literal: Daily the yamen gate stood empty and still, with no more litigants.
translations.idiomatic: Daily the yamen gate stood empty; no one came to sue.

sentences.zh: 其冬，醴泉出於界內。

translations.literal: That winter, sweet springs appeared within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: That winter sweet springs appeared within the borders.

sentences.zh: 及代至，傾城祖道。

translations.literal: When he was replaced and left, the whole city saw him off on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he was replaced, the whole city saw him off.

sentences.zh: 有老人丁金剛泣而前，謝曰：「己年九十，記三十五政，君非唯善治，清亦徹底。

translations.literal: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward, saying: "I am ninety and recall thirty-five administrations; my lord is not only skilled in rule—your clarity goes clean through.
translations.idiomatic: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward: "I am ninety and recall thirty-five administrations; you govern well, and your clarity goes clean through.

sentences.zh: 今失賢君，民何濟矣。

translations.literal: Now we lose a worthy lord—how shall the people be saved?
translations.idiomatic: Now we lose a worthy magistrate—how shall the people be saved?

sentences.zh: 」莫不攀援涕泣。

translations.literal: " None failed to cling and weep.
translations.idiomatic: " None failed to cling to him in tears.

sentences.zh: 除東郡太守，卒官。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Dong commandery and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Dong commandery and died in office.

sentences.zh: 世良強學，好屬文，撰《字略》五篇、《宋氏別錄》十卷。

translations.literal: Shiliang studied hard and loved composing text; he wrote Outline of Characters in five chapters and Song Clan Separate Records in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang studied hard and loved writing; he composed Outline of Characters in five chapters and Song Clan Separate Records in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 與弟世軌俱有孝友之譽。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Shigui both had a reputation for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Shigui both won fame for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 世軌，幼自嚴整，好法律，稍遷廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Shigui, from youth stern and orderly, loved the law; he was gradually promoted to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Shigui, stern from youth, loved the law and rose in time to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 洛州民聚結欲劫河橋，吏捕案之，連諸元徒黨千七百人。

translations.literal: The people of Luo province gathered intending to seize the Yellow River bridge; officials arrested and tried them, implicating more than seventeen hundred men of the Yuan clique and their associates.
translations.idiomatic: People of Luo province gathered to seize the Yellow River bridge; officials arrested them and implicated more than seventeen hundred Yuan clansmen and associates.

sentences.zh: 崔暹為廷尉，以之為反，數年不斷。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan was minister of justice and took it for rebellion; for years the case was not closed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan as minister of justice called it rebellion; for years the case would not close.

sentences.zh: 及世軌為少卿，判其事為劫。

translations.literal: When Shigui became vice minister, he judged the matter to be robbery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shigui became vice minister, he judged the matter robbery.

sentences.zh: 於是殺魁首，餘從坐悉舍焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ringleaders were executed and the rest who followed in guilt were all released.
translations.idiomatic: The ringleaders were executed; the rest were all released.

sentences.zh: 時大理正蘇珍之亦以平幹知名。

translations.literal: At the time the chief justice of the Court Su Zhenzhi was also known for balanced competence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Court chief justice Su Zhenzhi was also known for balanced competence.

sentences.zh: 寺中為之語曰：「決定嫌疑蘇珍之，視表見裏宋世軌。

translations.literal: Within the ministry they made a saying: "To decide doubtful guilt, Su Zhenzhi; to see the inside from the table, Song Shigui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministry they said: "To decide doubtful guilt—Su Zhenzhi; to see inside from the table—Song Shigui.

sentences.zh: 」時人以為寺中二絕。

translations.literal: " Men of the time took them as the ministry's twin marvels.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of the time called them the ministry's twin marvels.

sentences.zh: 南臺囚到廷尉，世軌多雪之。

translations.literal: Prisoners from the Southern Terrace arriving at the Court of Justice—Shigui often cleared them.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners sent from the Southern Terrace to the Court of Justice—Shigui often cleared them.

sentences.zh: 仍移攝御史，將問其濫狀，中尉畢義雲不送，移往復不止。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to investigating censor and was about to inquire into their abuses; the commandant Bi Yiyun would not deliver them, and though the transfer went back and forth it did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to investigating censor, he meant to inquire into their abuses; commandant Bi Yiyun would not hand prisoners over, and the exchanges would not end.

sentences.zh: 世軌遂上書，極言義雲酷擅。

translations.literal: Shigui then submitted a memorial, speaking to the utmost of Yiyun's cruel overreach.
translations.idiomatic: Shigui memorialized, denouncing Yiyun's cruel overreach to the full.

sentences.zh: 顯祖引見二人，親勑世軌曰：「我知臺欺寺久，卿能執理與之抗衡，但守此心，勿慮不富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong summoned the two men and in person charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; you can hold to principle and contend with them—only keep this heart and do not worry that you will not be rich and honored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong summoned both and told Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; hold to principle against them—keep this heart and you need not fear missing wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 」勑義雲曰：「卿比所為誠合死，以志在疾惡，故且一恕。

translations.literal: " He charged Yiyun: "What you have done of late truly deserves death; because your aim is to hate evil, for now you are pardoned once.
translations.idiomatic: " He told Yiyun: "Your recent conduct truly deserves death; because you aim to hate evil, you are pardoned once.

sentences.zh: 」仍顧謂朝臣曰：「此二人並我骨鯁臣也。

translations.literal: " He then turned to the court and said: "These two are both my bone-in-the-throat ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to the court: "These two are both ministers who stick in my throat.

sentences.zh: 」及疾卒，廷尉、御史諸繫囚聞世軌死，皆哭曰：「宋廷尉死，我等豈有生路！」

translations.literal: " When he died of illness, the imprisoned of the Court of Justice and the censorate, hearing Shigui was dead, all wept: "Minister Song of the Court is dead—where is our road to life!"
translations.idiomatic: " When he died, prisoners of the Court and censorate wept: "Court Minister Song is dead—where is our road to life?"

sentences.zh: 世良從子孝王，學涉，亦好緝綴文藻。

translations.literal: Shiliang's nephew Xiaowang was learned and also loved gathering and stitching literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang's nephew Xiaowang was learned and loved literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 形貌短陋，而好臧否人物，時論甚疾之。

translations.literal: His form was short and ugly, yet he loved to praise and blame men; opinion of the time greatly detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Short and ugly in form, he loved to praise and blame others; opinion of the time detested him.

sentences.zh: 為段孝言開府參軍，又薦為北平王文學。

translations.literal: He became staff officer to Duan Xiaoyan's opening office and was again recommended as literary officer to the Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He became staff officer in Duan Xiaoyan's opening office and was recommended as literary officer to the Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 求入文林館不遂，因非毀朝士，撰《別錄》二十卷，會平齊，改為《關東風俗傳》，更廣見聞，勒成三十卷以上之。

translations.literal: He sought entry into the Forest of Literature Hall and did not succeed; he therefore slandered court gentlemen and compiled Separate Records in twenty scrolls; when Qi was pacified he changed it to Eastern Pass Customs and Traditions, broadened what he had seen and heard, and presented more than thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Denied the Forest of Literature Hall, he slandered court gentlemen and compiled Separate Records in twenty scrolls; when Qi fell he retitled it Eastern Pass Customs and Traditions, broadened his material, and presented more than thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 言多妄謬，篇第冗雜，無著述體。

translations.literal: His words were mostly wild error; the sections were redundant and confused, without the form of real authorship.
translations.idiomatic: His words were mostly wild error; sections were redundant and confused, without real authorship.

sentences.zh: 郎基，字世業，中山人。

translations.literal: Lang Ji, style Shiye, was a man of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Ji, style Shiye, was from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，美鬚髯，泛涉墳典，尤長吏事。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall, with a fine beard; he ranged widely through the classics, especially skilled in clerkly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, with a fine beard, he ranged through the classics and excelled at administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，累遷海西鎮將。

translations.literal: He began his career as a court gentleman and was repeatedly promoted to defender of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a court gentleman and rose to defender of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 梁吳明徹率衆攻圍海西，基獎勵兵民，固守百餘日，軍糧且罄，戎仗亦盡，乃至削木為箭，剪紙為羽。

translations.literal: Liang's Wu Mingche led troops to besiege Haixi; Ji encouraged soldiers and people and firmly defended for more than a hundred days; army grain was nearly gone and weapons exhausted, until they even carved wood for arrows and cut paper for fletching.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche of Liang besieged Haixi; Ji encouraged soldiers and people and held firm for more than a hundred days until grain and arms were gone—they carved wood for arrows and cut paper for fletching.

sentences.zh: 圍解還朝，僕射楊愔迎勞之曰：「卿本文吏，遂有武略。

translations.literal: When the siege lifted and he returned to court, Vice Director Yang Yin met and comforted him, saying: "You were a civil clerk, yet had military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege lifted he returned; Vice Director Yang Yin met him: "You were a civil clerk, yet showed military strategy.

sentences.zh: 削木剪紙，皆無故事，班、墨之思，何以相過。」

translations.literal: Carving wood and cutting paper—there is no precedent for that; how could the thought of Ban and Mo be surpassed?"
translations.idiomatic: Carving wood and cutting paper has no precedent—how could Ban and Mo's inventiveness be surpassed?"

sentences.zh: 後帶潁川郡，積年留滯，數日之中，剖判咸盡，而臺報下，並允基所陳。

translations.literal: Later he held Yingchuan commandery concurrently; for years cases had stagnated, yet within days he judged and exhausted them all, and when the Terrace's reports came down they all accorded with what Ji had stated.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held Yingchuan concurrently; cases had stagnated for years, yet within days he cleared them all, and Terrace reports approved what Ji had ruled.

sentences.zh: 條綱旣疏，獄訟清息，官民遐邇，皆相慶悅。

translations.literal: The statutes were already sparse, litigation quiet, and officials and people far and near all rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes grew sparse, litigation quiet, and officials and people far and near rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 基性清慎，無所營求，曾語人云：「任官之所，木枕亦不須作，況重於此事。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was pure and cautious, with nothing he sought for himself; he once told others: "Where one serves in office, one need not even make a wooden pillow—how much less anything heavier than that.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and cautious, he sought nothing for himself; he once said: "In office one need not even make a wooden pillow—how much less anything beyond that.

sentences.zh: 」唯頗令寫書。

translations.literal: " He only rather ordered books copied.
translations.idiomatic: " He only had books copied.

sentences.zh: 潘子義曾遺之書曰：「在官寫書，亦是風流罪過。

translations.literal: Pan Ziyi once sent him a letter saying: "To copy books in office is also a frivolous fault of fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Ziyi wrote: "Copying books in office is also a fashionable fault.

sentences.zh: 」基答書曰：「觀過知仁，斯亦可矣。

translations.literal: " Ji answered: "To see fault and know benevolence—that too will do.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji replied: "To see fault and know benevolence—that will do.

sentences.zh: 」後卒官，柩將還，遠近將送，莫不攀轅悲哭。

translations.literal: " Later he died in office; when the coffin was to return, those far and near who escorted him none failed to cling to the carriage rails and weep.
translations.idiomatic: " He later died in office; when the coffin was to return, escorts far and near clung to the carriage rails in tears.

sentences.zh: 孟業，字敬業，鉅鹿安國人。

translations.literal: Meng Ye, style Jingye, was a man of Anguo in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ye, style Jingye, was from Anguo in Julu.

sentences.zh: 家本寒微，少為州吏。

translations.literal: His family was originally poor and low; in youth he was a provincial clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; in youth he was a provincial clerk.

sentences.zh: 性廉謹，同僚諸人侵盜官絹，分三十疋與之，拒而不受。

translations.literal: His nature was honest and cautious; colleagues who stole official silk divided thirty bolts for him and he refused and would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Honest and cautious, when colleagues who stole official silk offered him thirty bolts he refused.

sentences.zh: 魏彭城王韶拜定州，除典籖。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Pengcheng Shao was appointed to Ding province and made Ye records-and-keeper.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Prince of Pengcheng Shao took Ding province, Ye was made records-and-keeper.

sentences.zh: 長史劉仁之謂業曰：「我處其外，君居其內，同心戮力，庶有濟乎。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Liu Renzhi said to Ye: "I stand outside, you dwell within; with one heart and shared strength, perhaps there can be success.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Liu Renzhi told Ye: "I stand outside, you within; with one heart we may succeed.

sentences.zh: 」未幾仁之徵入為中書令，臨路啟韶云：「殿下左右可信任者唯有孟業，願專任之。

translations.literal: " Before long Renzhi was summoned in as director of the Secretariat; on the road he told Shao: "Among those around Your Highness whom you can trust there is only Meng Ye—wish to put sole trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Renzhi was summoned to the Secretariat; leaving, he told Shao: "Of those around you, only Meng Ye can be trusted—put sole trust in him.

sentences.zh: 餘人不可信也。

translations.literal: The rest cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The rest cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 」又與業別，執手曰：「今我出都，君便失援，恐君在後，不自保全。

translations.literal: " He also parted from Ye, took his hand, and said: "Now I leave the capital and you lose support; I fear that afterward you cannot preserve yourself.
translations.idiomatic: " Parting from Ye he took his hand: "I leave the capital and you lose support; I fear you cannot preserve yourself afterward.

sentences.zh: 唯正與直，願君自勉。

translations.literal: Only uprightness and straightness—wish you to urge yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Only uprightness and straightness—urge yourself.

sentences.zh: 」業唯有一馬，因瘦而死。

translations.literal: " Ye had only one horse; it died from thinness.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye had only one horse; it died from thinness.

sentences.zh: 韶以業家貧，令州府官人同食馬肉，欲令厚償，業固辭不敢。

translations.literal: Shao, because Ye's family was poor, ordered the provincial and commandery officials to eat the horse's flesh together, wishing to give generous compensation; Ye firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ye's family was poor, Shao ordered officials to eat the horse's flesh and meant to compensate him generously; Ye firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 韶乃戲業曰：「卿邀名人也。

translations.literal: Shao then jested to Ye: "You invite a famous man's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao jested: "You court a famous man's reputation.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「業以微細，伏事節下，旣不能裨益，寧可損敗清風。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Ye is minute and low, serving Your Highness in attendance; since I cannot benefit you, how could I damage your clear wind?
translations.idiomatic: " Ye answered: "I am minute and low, serving in attendance; since I cannot benefit you, how could I damage your clear reputation?

sentences.zh: 」後高祖書與韶云：「典籖姓孟者極能用心，何不置之目前。

translations.literal: " Later Gao Huan wrote to Shao: "The records-keeper surnamed Meng is extremely able in intent—why not place him before your eyes.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Gao Huan wrote Shao: "The records-keeper surnamed Meng is extremely attentive—why not keep him before your eyes?

sentences.zh: 」韶，高祖之婿也。

translations.literal: " Shao was Gao Huan's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao was Gao Huan's son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 仁之後為兗州，臨別謂吏部崔暹曰：「貴州人士，唯有孟業，宜銓舉之，他人不可信也。

translations.literal: After Ren became governor of Yanzhou, on parting he said to Personnel Director Cui Xian: "Among the province's men, only Meng Ye should be selected and recommended; others cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren later became governor of Yanzhou, he took leave of Personnel Director Cui Xian and said, "Of the men in this province, only Meng Ye deserves selection and promotion; the rest are not to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 」崔暹問業曰：「君往在定州，有何政績，使劉西兗如此欽歎？

translations.literal: " Cui Xian asked Ye: "When you were in Dingzhou, what achievements made Liu of Western Yanzhou admire you so?
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Xian asked Ye, "When you were in Dingzhou, what achievements made Liu of Western Yanzhou admire you so?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「稟性愚直，唯知自修，無他長也。」

translations.literal: " He answered: "By nature I am blunt and straight; I only know how to cultivate myself—no other strengths."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "By nature I am blunt and honest; I only know how to improve myself—I have no other talents."

sentences.zh: 天保初，清河王岳拜司州牧，聞業名行，復召為法曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Prince of Qinghe Yue was appointed governor of Si Province; hearing of Ye's reputation and conduct, he again summoned him as legal-affairs officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, Prince of Qinghe Yue became governor of Si Province; hearing Ye's reputation, he summoned him again as legal-affairs officer.

sentences.zh: 業形貌短小，及謁見，岳心鄙其眇小，笑而不言。

translations.literal: Ye's stature was short; when he came to audience, Yue inwardly despised his small size and laughed without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was short in stature; at their audience Yue inwardly scorned his slight build and laughed without a word.

sentences.zh: 後尋業斷決之處，乃謂業曰：「卿斷決之明，可謂有過軀貌之用。

translations.literal: Later, upon reviewing cases Ye had decided, he said to Ye: "Your clarity in judgment can be said to exceed what your body suggests.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after examining Ye's rulings, he told him, "Your clarity in judgment exceeds what your stature would suggest."

sentences.zh: 」尋遷東郡守，以寬惠著。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to administrator of Dong commandery, where he became known for lenience and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrator of Dong commandery, where he became known for lenience and kindness.

sentences.zh: 其年，麥一莖五穗，其餘三穗四穗共一莖，合郡人以為政化所感。

translations.literal: That year, one stalk of wheat bore five ears; the rest had three or four ears on one stalk—the whole commandery took it as a response to his transforming government.
translations.idiomatic: That year one wheat stalk bore five ears, while others bore three or four on a single stalk; the whole commandery regarded it as a sign of his transforming rule.

sentences.zh: 尋以病卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 崔伯謙，字士遜，博陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Boqian, styled Shixun, was a man of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Boqian, styled Shixun, came from Boling.

sentences.zh: 父文業，鉅鹿守。

translations.literal: His father Wenyue was administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenyue had been administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 伯謙少孤貧，善養母。

translations.literal: Boqian was orphaned young and poor, yet good at supporting his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, Boqian was devoted to supporting his mother.

sentences.zh: 高祖召赴晉陽，補相府功曹，稱之曰：「清直奉公，真良佐也。

translations.literal: Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang and appointed him staff merit officer in the chancellor's office, praising him: "Upright, pure, and devoted to public duty—a true fine assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang and made him staff merit officer in the chancellor's office, saying, "Pure, upright, and devoted to the public—he is a true fine assistant."

sentences.zh: 」遷瀛州別駕。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to vice governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 世宗以為京畿司馬，勞之曰：「卿騁足瀛部，已著康歌，督府務殷，是用相授。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng made him metropolitan-area marshal and comforted him: "You have galloped through the Ying region and already won songs of praise; the supervisory office's duties are heavy—therefore I entrust this to you.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng made him metropolitan-area marshal and told him, "You have already distinguished yourself in the Ying region and won popular praise; the supervisory office's business is heavy—so I entrust this post to you."

sentences.zh: 」族弟暹，當時寵要，謙與之僚舊同門，非吉兇，未曾造請。

translations.literal: " His clansman Xian was then in favor and power; Boqian had been his colleague and schoolmate, yet except for good or ill fortune he never paid a visit.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xian then held favor and power; though they had been colleagues and schoolmates, Boqian never called on him except for weddings or funerals.

sentences.zh: 後除濟北太守，恩信大行，乃改鞭用熟皮為之，不忍見血，示恥而已。

translations.literal: Later he was made administrator of Jibei; kindness and trust spread widely, and he changed the whip to one made of soft tanned leather, unwilling to see blood—shame alone was the point.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed administrator of Jibei, he won wide trust through kindness and replaced the whip with one of soft tanned leather, unwilling to draw blood—shame alone was the aim.

sentences.zh: 有朝貴行過郡境，問人太守治政何如。

translations.literal: A court noble passing through the commandery asked how the administrator governed.
translations.idiomatic: A court noble traveling through the commandery asked how the prefect governed.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「府君恩化，古者所無。

translations.literal: The reply was: "Our lord's gracious transforming power is like nothing in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Our lord's gracious rule is unlike anything of old.

sentences.zh: 因誦民為歌曰：『崔府君，能治政，易鞭鞭，布威德，民無爭。

translations.literal: Then they recited the people's song: 'Prefect Cui can govern well; change the whip, spread authority and virtue, and the people do not quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: They recited the people's song: "Prefect Cui governs well; change the whip, spread authority and virtue, and the people do not quarrel."

sentences.zh: 』」客曰：「旣稱恩化，何由復威？

translations.literal: '" The guest said: "If you call it gracious transforming power, how can there also be authority?
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "If you call it gracious rule, how can there also be authority?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「長吏憚威，民庶蒙惠。

translations.literal: " The reply was: "Senior officials fear his authority; the common people receive his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Officials fear his authority; common people receive his kindness."

sentences.zh: 」徵赴鄴，百姓號泣遮道。

translations.literal: " When he was summoned to Ye, the people wept and blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to Ye, the people wept and blocked the road.

sentences.zh: 以弟讓在關中，不復居內任，除南鉅鹿守，事無巨細，必自親覽。

translations.literal: Because his brother Rang was in Guanzhong, he no longer held an inner appointment and was made administrator of southern Julu; in affairs great or small he always examined them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because his brother Rang was in Guanzhong, he took no further inner post and was made administrator of southern Julu, personally reviewing every matter large or small.

sentences.zh: 民有貧弱未理者，皆曰：「我自有白鬚公，不慮不決。

translations.literal: When the people were poor or weak and their cases unsettled, all said: "We have our White-Beard Lord—we need not worry that it will not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: If the poor and weak had cases unsettled, they all said, "We have our White-Beard Lord—we need not worry it will go undecided."

sentences.zh: 」後為銀青光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: " Later he became silver-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later became silver-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue and died.

sentences.zh: 蘇瓊，字珍之，武強人也。

translations.literal: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, was a man of Wuqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, came from Wuqiang.

sentences.zh: 父備，仕魏至衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: His father Bei served Wei up to vice minister of the court of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bei served Wei as far as vice minister of the court of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 瓊幼時隨父在邊，嘗謁東荊州刺史曹芝。

translations.literal: When Qiong was young he followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Qiong followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 芝戲問曰：「卿欲官不？

translations.literal: Zhi asked in jest: "Do you want an office?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi asked playfully, "Do you want an office?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「設官求人，非人求官。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Offices are set up to seek men—not men to seek offices.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Offices are established to seek men, not men to seek offices."

sentences.zh: 」芝異其對，署為府長流參軍。

translations.literal: " Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.

sentences.zh: 文襄以儀同開府，引為刑獄參軍，每加勉勞。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng, with the rank of palace guard of the fifth order, opened a staff office and brought him in as penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging and commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng, holding the rank of fifth-order palace guard, opened a staff office and made him penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 幷州嘗有強盜，長流參軍推其事，所疑賊並已拷伏，失物家並識認，唯不獲盜贓。

translations.literal: Bing province once had bandits; the senior adjutant investigated the matter, and all the suspected thieves had already confessed under torture; the owners of the lost goods all identified them, yet the stolen goods were not recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In Bing Province there had been bandits; the senior adjutant investigated, and every suspect had confessed under torture while the owners identified them—yet the stolen goods were never found.

sentences.zh: 文襄付瓊更令窮審，乃別推得元景融等十餘人，並獲贓驗。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng handed the case to Qiong for a further exhaustive inquiry; he then traced it separately and obtained Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others, all with stolen goods verified.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng put Qiong on a fresh exhaustive inquiry; he traced the case separately and found Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others, all with the loot recovered.

sentences.zh: 文襄大笑，語前妄引賊者曰：「爾輩若不遇我好參軍，幾致枉死。」

translations.literal: Gao Cheng laughed loudly and said to those who had earlier wrongly implicated the thieves: "If you had not met my fine staff officer, you would nearly have died wrongfully."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng laughed and told those who had wrongly implicated the thieves, "If you had not met my fine staff officer, you would almost have been executed unjustly."

sentences.zh: 除南清河太守，其郡多盜，及瓊至，民吏肅然，姦盜止息。

translations.literal: He was made administrator of southern Qinghe; the commandery had many thieves, but when Qiong arrived officials and people became orderly and wicked theft ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed administrator of southern Qinghe, a commandery rife with thieves, he brought officials and people to order and wicked theft ceased.

sentences.zh: 或外境姦非，輒從界中行過者，無不捉送。

translations.literal: If wrongdoing from outside the borders passed through his territory, none failed to be seized and sent in.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongdoers from neighboring districts who passed through his borders were invariably seized and delivered.

sentences.zh: 零陵縣民魏雙成失牛，疑其村人魏子賓，送至郡，一經窮問，知賓非盜者，卽便放之。

translations.literal: A man of Lingling county, Wei Shuangcheng, lost an ox and suspected his fellow villager Wei Zibin; he was sent to the commandery, and after one thorough questioning it was known Zibin was not the thief, so he was immediately released.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuangcheng of Lingling county lost an ox and suspected Wei Zibin of his village; Zibin was sent to the commandery, and after one thorough inquiry Qiong knew he was not the thief and released him at once.

sentences.zh: 雙成訴云：「府君放賊去，百姓牛何處可得？

translations.literal: Shuangcheng complained: "The prefect let the thief go—where are the common people's oxen to come from?
translations.idiomatic: Shuangcheng complained, "The prefect let the thief go—how are ordinary people to recover their oxen?"

sentences.zh: 」瓊不理，密走私訪，別獲盜者。

translations.literal: " Qiong paid no heed and secretly sent private inquiries, separately catching the real thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong ignored him, sent private inquiries, and separately caught the real thieves.

sentences.zh: 從此畜牧不收，多放散，云：「但付府君。

translations.literal: From then on people no longer penned their livestock but mostly let them roam free, saying: "Just leave them to the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After that people often stopped penning livestock and let herds roam free, saying, "Just leave them to the prefect."

sentences.zh: 」有鄰郡富豪將財物寄置界內以避盜，為賊攻急，告曰：「我物已寄蘇公矣。

translations.literal: " A rich man of a neighboring commandery placed goods within the border to avoid thieves; when bandits pressed him hard he said: "My goods are already lodged with Lord Su.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man from a neighboring commandery stored goods inside the border to escape thieves; when bandits pressed him he said, "My goods are already with Lord Su."

sentences.zh: 」賊遂去。

translations.literal: " The bandits then left.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 平原郡有妖賊劉黑狗，構結徒侶，通於滄海。

translations.literal: In Pingyuan commandery there was a demonic bandit, Liu Heigou, who gathered followers and had ties to the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: In Pingyuan commandery a demonic bandit, Liu Heigou, gathered followers with ties to the eastern sea.

sentences.zh: 瓊所部人連接村居，無相染累。

translations.literal: Where Qiong's people lived in connected villages along the border, none were infected or implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Villages along Qiong's border that adjoined the bandits' territory suffered no infection or implicated cases.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑於此伏其德。

translations.literal: Neighboring districts at this submitted to his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring districts thereby submitted to his virtue.

sentences.zh: 郡中舊賊一百餘人，悉充左右，人間善惡，及長吏飲人一杯酒，無不卽知。

translations.literal: More than a hundred old thieves in the commandery he all made his attendants; good and ill among the people, and even when a senior official drank one cup of wine with someone—nothing failed to reach him at once.
translations.idiomatic: He took more than a hundred former thieves in the commandery as his attendants; good and ill among the people, and even when a senior official shared a cup of wine with someone—nothing failed to reach him at once.

sentences.zh: 瓊性清慎，不發私書。

translations.literal: Qiong's nature was pure and cautious; he never sent private letters.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was pure and cautious by nature and never sent private letters.

sentences.zh: 道人道研為濟州沙門統，資產巨富，在郡多有出息，常得郡縣為徵。

translations.literal: The monk Daoyan was Buddhist superintendent of Jizhou, with vast wealth; in the commandery he had much income and often had the commandery and counties collect for him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Daoyan, Buddhist superintendent of Jizhou, was hugely wealthy and had many income streams in the commandery, often collected through county and commandery offices.

sentences.zh: 及欲求謁，度知其意，每見則談問玄理，應對肅敬，研雖為債數來，無由啟口。

translations.literal: When he wished to call and pay respects, Qiong knew his intent; each meeting he would discuss abstruse principles, answering with solemn respect—though Daoyan came many times on debt matters, he had no way to open his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyan wished to call on him, Qiong knew his intent; at each meeting he discussed abstruse principles with solemn respect—though Daoyan came repeatedly on debt business, he never found an opening.

sentences.zh: 其弟子問其故，研曰：「每見府君，徑將我入青雲間，何由得論地上事。

translations.literal: His disciples asked the reason; Daoyan said: "Each time I see the prefect he carries me straight into the blue clouds—how can I discuss earthly affairs?
translations.idiomatic: His disciples asked why; Daoyan said, "Each time I see the prefect he carries me straight into the blue clouds—how can I speak of earthly affairs?"

sentences.zh: 」郡民趙潁曾為樂陵太守，八十致事歸。

translations.literal: " A man of the commandery, Zhao Ying, had once been administrator of Leling; at eighty he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery man, Zhao Ying, had been administrator of Leling; at eighty he retired home.

sentences.zh: 五月初，得新瓜一雙自來送。

translations.literal: In early fifth month he brought a pair of fresh melons as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: In early fifth month he brought a pair of fresh melons as a gift.

sentences.zh: 潁恃年老，苦請，遂便為留，仍致於聽事梁上，竟不剖。

translations.literal: Ying, relying on his age, pressed hard; Qiong finally kept them and hung them on a beam in the reception hall, never cutting them open.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, relying on his age, pressed hard; Qiong finally kept them and hung them on a beam in the reception hall without ever cutting them.

sentences.zh: 人遂競貢新果，至門，聞知潁瓜猶在，相顧而去。

translations.literal: People then competed to offer fresh fruit; reaching the gate and hearing Ying's melons were still there, they looked at one another and left.
translations.idiomatic: People then vied to offer fresh fruit; at the gate, learning Ying's melons were still there, they looked at one another and left.

sentences.zh: 有百姓乙普明兄弟爭田，積年不斷，各相援引，乃至百人。

translations.literal: Commoners Yi Puming and his brothers disputed fields; for years it was unsettled; each side cited supporters until there were nearly a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners Yi Puming and his brothers disputed fields for years without settlement, each side citing supporters until the case involved nearly a hundred people.

sentences.zh: 瓊召普明兄弟對衆人諭之曰：「天下難得者兄弟，易求者田地，假令得地失兄弟心如何？

translations.literal: Qiong summoned the Puming brothers before the crowd and instructed them: "What the world can scarcely obtain is brothers; what is easy to seek is fields—suppose you gain land but lose your brothers' hearts, how then?
translations.idiomatic: Qiong summoned the brothers before the crowd and said, "Brothers are what the world can scarcely obtain; fields are easy to find—if you gain land but lose your brothers' hearts, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」因而下灑，從人莫不淚泣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears fell; none among those present failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Tears fell from his eyes; none among those present failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 普明弟兄叩頭乞外更思，分異十年，遂還同住。

translations.literal: The Puming brothers knocked their heads and begged to withdraw and reconsider; separated for ten years, they then returned to live together.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers kowtowed and begged to withdraw and reconsider; separated ten years, they then returned to live together.

sentences.zh: 每年春，總集大儒衛覬隆、田元鳳等講於郡學，朝吏文案之暇，悉令受書，時人指吏曹為學生屋。

translations.literal: Every spring he gathered great Confucians Wei Jilong, Tian Yuanfeng, and others to lecture at the commandery school; when court clerks had spare time from documents, he had them all study books—people of the time called the clerks' quarters the students' hall.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring he gathered great Confucians Wei Jilong, Tian Yuanfeng, and others to lecture at the commandery school; in spare moments from documents he had all court clerks study—people called the clerks' quarters the students' hall.

sentences.zh: 禁斷淫祠，婚姻喪葬皆教令儉而中禮。

translations.literal: He forbade licentious shrines; marriages and funerals were all taught to be frugal yet within ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade improper shrines and taught weddings and funerals to be frugal yet within ritual.

sentences.zh: 又蠶月預下綿絹度樣於部內，其兵賦次第並立明式，至於調役，事必先辦，郡縣長吏常無十杖稽失。

translations.literal: Also, in silkworm month he sent down silk-gauze quota samples throughout the district; military levies and their order were all set in clear forms; as for corvée and requisitions, matters were always prepared in advance—the commandery and county administrators often had not even ten blows' penalty for delay.
translations.idiomatic: In silkworm month he issued silk-gauze quota samples throughout the district; military levies were set in clear order; corvée and requisitions were always prepared in advance—commandery and county heads often had not even ten blows' penalty for delay.

sentences.zh: 當時州郡無不遣人至境，訪其政術。

translations.literal: At the time no province or commandery failed to send men to his border to inquire into his methods of government.
translations.idiomatic: At the time every province and commandery sent men to his border to study his methods of government.

sentences.zh: 天保中，郡界大水，人災，絕食者千餘家。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era great floods struck the commandery borders; there was human disaster, and more than a thousand households were without food.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao, great floods struck the commandery; more than a thousand households were left without food.

sentences.zh: 瓊普集部中有粟家，自從貸粟以給付饑者。

translations.literal: Qiong broadly gathered households in the district that had grain and personally borrowed grain from them to supply the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong gathered every household in the district that had grain and personally borrowed from them to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 州計戶徵租，復欲推其貸粟。

translations.literal: The province counted households to levy tax and again wished to assess his borrowed grain.
translations.idiomatic: The province counted households for tax levy and again sought to assess his borrowed grain.

sentences.zh: 綱紀謂瓊曰：「雖矜饑餧，恐罪累府君。

translations.literal: The clerks said to Qiong: "Though you pity the starving, I fear guilt will fall on the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His clerks told him, "Though you pity the starving, I fear the guilt will fall on you, my lord."

sentences.zh: 」瓊曰：「一身獲罪，且活千室，何所怨乎？

translations.literal: " Qiong said: "One body may incur guilt, yet a thousand households live—what is there to resent?
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said, "One body may bear guilt, yet a thousand households live—what is there to resent?"

sentences.zh: 」遂上表陳狀，使檢皆免，人戶保安。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized stating the facts, had the investigation all remitted, and households and people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the facts, had the investigation remitted entirely, and households were kept secure.

sentences.zh: 此等相撫兒子，咸言府君生汝。

translations.literal: Those he had fostered as sons all said the prefect gave you birth.
translations.idiomatic: Those he had fostered as sons all said, "The prefect gave you birth."

sentences.zh: 在郡六年，人庶懷之，遂無一人經州。

translations.literal: In the commandery six years, the people cherished him, and not one person brought a case to the province.
translations.idiomatic: For six years in the commandery the people cherished him, and not one person brought a case to the province.

sentences.zh: 前後四表，列為尤最。

translations.literal: Four memorials in succession ranked him foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Four successive memorials ranked him foremost.

sentences.zh: 遭憂解職，故人贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: When mourning obliged him to leave office, gifts from old friends—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning obliged him to leave office, he accepted none of the gifts old friends offered.

sentences.zh: 尋起為司直、廷尉正，朝士嗟其屈。

translations.literal: Soon he was reappointed rectifier and director of the Court of Justice; court gentlemen sighed that he was held down.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed rectifier and director of the Court of Justice; court gentlemen sighed that he was underused.

sentences.zh: 尚書辛述曰：「旣直且正，名以定體，不慮不申。」

translations.literal: Master of Writing Xin Shu said: "Upright and also correct—the name fixes the substance; no worry that it will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Xin Shu said, "Upright and correct—his name fixes his substance; there is no worry he will not prevail."

sentences.zh: 初，瓊任清河太守，裴獻伯為濟州刺史，酷於用法，瓊恩於養人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qiong was administrator of Qinghe, Pei Xianbo was inspector of Jizhou, harsh in applying the law, while Qiong was kind in nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qiong was administrator of Qinghe, Pei Xianbo was inspector of Jizhou, harsh in applying the law, while Qiong was kind in nurturing people.

sentences.zh: 房延佑為樂陵郡，過州，裴問其外聲，佑云：「唯聞太守善，刺史惡。

translations.literal: Fang Yanyou was administrator of Leling; passing through the province, Pei asked about outside reputation; You said: "I only hear that the administrator is good and the inspector is bad.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanyou was administrator of Leling; passing through the province, Pei asked outside reputation; You said, "I only hear the administrator is praised and the inspector is condemned."

sentences.zh: 」裴云：「得民譽者非至公。

translations.literal: " Pei said: "One who wins the people's praise is not utterly impartial.
translations.idiomatic: Pei said, "One who wins popular praise is not utterly impartial."

sentences.zh: 」佑答言：「若爾，黃霸、龔遂君之罪人也。

translations.literal: " You answered: "If so, then Huang Ba and Gong Sui were your sort of criminal.
translations.idiomatic: You replied, "If that is so, then Huang Ba and Gong Sui were criminals by your standard."

sentences.zh: 」後有勑，州各舉清能。

translations.literal: " Later there was an edict that each province should recommend the pure and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered each province to recommend the pure and capable.

sentences.zh: 裴以前言，恐為瓊陷，瓊申其枉滯，議者尚其公平。

translations.literal: Because of his earlier words, Pei feared Qiong would trap him; Qiong stated his wrongful detention, and commentators respected his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his earlier remark Pei feared Qiong would trap him; Qiong stated his wrongful detention, and commentators respected his fairness.

sentences.zh: 畢義雲為御史中丞，以猛暴任職，理官忌憚，莫敢有違。

translations.literal: Bi Yiyun was censor-in-chief; fierce and violent in office, legal officials feared him and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yiyun was censor-in-chief, fierce and violent in office; legal officials feared him and none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 瓊推察務在公平，得雪者甚衆，寺署臺案，始自於瓊。

translations.literal: Qiong's investigations aimed at fairness; those cleared were very many—court and censorate cases began with Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's investigations aimed at fairness; very many were cleared—court and censorate cases began with Qiong.

sentences.zh: 遷三公郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to gentleman of the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the three offices.

sentences.zh: 趙州及清河、南中有人頻告謀反，前後皆付瓊推撿，事多申雪。

translations.literal: In Zhao province and Qinghe and southern Zhong, people repeatedly reported plots of rebellion; case after case was handed to Qiong for investigation, and many were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhao province, Qinghe, and southern Zhong people repeatedly reported rebellion; case after case went to Qiong for investigation, and many were cleared.

sentences.zh: 尚書崔昂謂瓊曰：「若欲立功名，當更思餘理，仍數雪反逆，身命何輕？

translations.literal: Master of Writing Cui Ang said to Qiong: "If you wish to establish merit and fame, you should think of other principles; still repeatedly clearing treason cases—how lightly you hold your life?
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Cui Ang told Qiong, "If you wish merit and fame, you should think of other principles; you still repeatedly clear treason cases—how lightly you hold your life?"

sentences.zh: 」瓊正色曰：「所雪者怨枉，不放反逆。

translations.literal: " Qiong said sternly: "What I clear are wrongful grievances—I do not release real rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said sternly, "What I clear are wrongful grievances—I do not release real rebels."

sentences.zh: 」昂大慚。

translations.literal: " Ang was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 京師為之語曰：「斷決無疑蘇珍之。

translations.literal: The capital had a saying: "Judgment without doubt—Su Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had a saying: "Judgment without doubt—Su Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 」遷左丞，行徐州事。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to left vice director and acted in Xu province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to left vice director and acted in Xu province affairs.

sentences.zh: 徐州城中五級寺忽被盜銅像一百軀，有司徵檢，四鄰防宿及蹤跡所疑，逮系數十人，瓊一時放遣。

translations.literal: In Xu province city the Five-Tier Temple was suddenly robbed of a hundred bronze statues; the relevant office investigated; neighbors on night watch and those suspected by tracks—several tens were seized and bound; Qiong released them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuzhou city the Five-Tier Temple was robbed of a hundred bronze statues; the authorities investigated neighbors on night watch and everyone suspicion touched—several tens were seized; Qiong released them all at once.

sentences.zh: 寺僧怨訴不為推賊，瓊遣僧，謝曰：「但且還寺，得像自送。

translations.literal: The temple monks complained that he did not pursue the thieves; Qiong sent the monks away, saying: "Just return to the temple—the statues will deliver themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The monks complained he did not pursue the thieves; Qiong sent them away, saying, "Just return to the temple—the statues will come back on their own."

sentences.zh: 」爾後十日，抄賊姓名及贓處所，徑收掩，悉獲實驗，賊徒款引，道俗歎伏。

translations.literal: " Ten days later he had the bandits' names and where the loot was hidden, went straight to seize them, all verified in fact; the thieves confessed in detail, and clergy and laity sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he had the bandits' names and the hiding places, seized them directly, verified everything, and the thieves confessed in detail—monks and laypeople alike marveled.

sentences.zh: 舊制以淮禁不聽商販輒度，淮南歲儉，啟聽淮北取糴。

translations.literal: By old regulation the Huai prohibition did not allow merchants to cross at will; when Huainan had a lean year, Qiong memorialized to allow buying grain north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation the Huai crossing barred merchants at will; when Huainan had a lean year, Qiong memorialized to allow buying grain north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 後淮北人饑，復請通糴淮南，遂得商估往還，彼此兼濟，水陸之利，通於河北。

translations.literal: Later when people north of the Huai were hungry, he again requested open grain trade with Huainan; merchants could then go back and forth, each region aiding the other, and the profit of water and land routes reached Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Later when north Huai people were hungry, he again requested open grain trade with Huainan; merchants went back and forth, each side aiding the other, and water and land routes profited Hebei.

sentences.zh: 後為大理卿而齊亡，仕周為博陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he became director of the Court of Justice, but Qi perished; he served Zhou as administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He later became director of the Court of Justice, but Qi fell; he served Zhou as administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 房豹，字仲幹，清河人。

translations.literal: Fang Bao, styled Zhonggan, was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bao, styled Zhonggan, came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖法壽，《魏書》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fashou has a biography in the Book of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fashou has a biography in the Book of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父翼宗。

translations.literal: His father was Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yizong.

sentences.zh: 豹體貌魁岸，美音儀。

translations.literal: Bao's physique was lofty and imposing; his voice and bearing were fine.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was tall and broad-shouldered, with a handsome voice and bearing.

sentences.zh: 釋褐開府參軍，兼行臺郎中，隨慕容紹宗。

translations.literal: Upon doffing the hemp he became an opening-office staff officer, concurrently mobile-office gentleman, and followed Murong Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: He doffed the hemp and entered service as an opening-office staff officer and concurrent mobile-office gentleman, attending Murong Shaozong.

sentences.zh: 紹宗自云有水厄，遂於戰艦中浴，並自投於水，冀以厭當之。

translations.literal: Shaozong said himself that he had a water bane; he therefore bathed in the war galley and also threw himself into the water, hoping to use repellence to meet and counter it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong claimed a water bane was upon him, so he bathed aboard the war galley and even threw himself into the river, hoping an apotropaic counter-measure would turn fate aside.

sentences.zh: 豹曰：「夫命也在天，豈人理所能延促？

translations.literal: Bao said, "Fate lies in Heaven—can human reason shorten or lengthen it?
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "Fate is Heaven's to give—what mortal scheme could hurry or delay it?

sentences.zh: 公若實有災眚，恐非禳所能解；

translations.literal: If my lord truly has disaster and bane, I fear averting rites cannot resolve it;
translations.idiomatic: If you truly face disaster, I doubt any averting rite can lift it;

sentences.zh: 若其實無，何禳之有。

translations.literal: if in truth there is none, what is there to avert?
translations.idiomatic: if there is none in truth, what would you avert?

sentences.zh: 」紹宗笑曰：「不能免俗，聊復爾耳。

translations.literal: " Shaozong laughed and said, "One cannot escape vulgar custom—for a little while one does the same again.
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Shaozong laughed. "Cannot escape the vulgar," he said; "one goes through the motions, that is all.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而紹宗遇溺，時論以為知微。

translations.literal: " Before long Shaozong met drowning; commentators of the time held that Bao had known the subtle sign.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Murong Shaozong drowned; opinion at the time took it that Bao had read the omen.

sentences.zh: 遷樂陵太守，鎮以凝重，哀矜貧弱。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Leling; he governed with weight and solemnity, pitying the poor and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to administrator of Leling, he ruled with grave steadiness and pitied the poor and weak.

sentences.zh: 豹階庭簡靜，圄囹空虛。

translations.literal: Under Bao the court and courtyard were plain and quiet; the prisons stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Under Bao the yamen stayed plain and quiet and the cells stood empty.

sentences.zh: 郡治瀕海，水味多鹹苦，豹命鑿一井，遂得甘泉，遐邇以為政化所致。

translations.literal: The commandery seat lay by the sea; the water tasted mostly salty and bitter. Bao ordered a well dug, and sweet spring was obtained; far and near took it as caused by his transforming governance.
translations.idiomatic: The seat lay on the coast, where the water ran salty and bitter. Bao had a well sunk and sweet water rose; people far and near credited his transforming rule.

sentences.zh: 豹罷歸後，井味復鹹。

translations.literal: After Bao left office and returned home, the well's taste turned salty again.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bao had left office and gone home, the well turned salty again.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，還鄉園自養，頻徵，辭疾。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed, he returned to his home estate to nourish himself; summons came repeatedly, but he pleaded illness and declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he went home to tend his estate. Summons came again and again; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 終於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 路去病，陽平人也。

translations.literal: Lu Qubing was a man of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qubing was a native of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 風神疏朗，儀表瓌異。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were open and clear; his appearance was singular and striking.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was open and lucid; his looks were singular and striking.

sentences.zh: 釋褐開府參軍。

translations.literal: Upon doffing the hemp he became an opening-office staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He doffed the hemp and became an opening-office staff officer.

sentences.zh: 勑用士人為縣宰，以去病為定州饒陽令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that literati be used as county magistrates; Qubing was made Magistrate of Raoyang in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required that cultivated men serve as county magistrates, and Qubing was appointed magistrate of Raoyang in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 去病明閑時務，性頗嚴毅，人不敢欺，然至廉平，為吏民嘆服。

translations.literal: Qubing was clear and adept in affairs of the time; his nature was rather stern and firm—men did not dare deceive him, yet he was utterly fair and incorrupt, and officials and commoners alike sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing understood the affairs of the age and was by nature stern and firm; none dared cheat him, yet he was utterly fair, and officials and commoners alike marveled.

sentences.zh: 擢為成安令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Cheng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Cheng'an.

sentences.zh: 京城下有鄴、臨漳、成安三縣，輦轂之下，舊號難治，重以政亂時難，綱維不立，功臣內戚，請囑百端。

translations.literal: Near the capital lay three counties—Ye, Linzhang, and Cheng'an. Under the chariot-hub they had long been called hard to govern; compounded by chaotic government and hard times, the net of law was not established, and meritorious ministers and imperial affines made requests from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Below the capital stood Ye, Linzhang, and Cheng'an—three counties long notorious under the imperial hub. Disorder piled on hard times; law's net hung slack, and meritorious ministers and imperial kin pressed requests from every side.

sentences.zh: 去病消息事宜，以理抗答，勢要之徒，雖廝養小人莫不憚其風格，亦不至嫌恨。

translations.literal: Qubing kept himself informed of affairs and answered requests with reason; men of power—even grooms and petty servants—all feared his integrity of style, yet none came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing tracked every matter and answered on principle. Men of influence—even grooms and petty servants—feared his bearing, yet none bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 自遷鄴以還，三縣令治術，去病獨為稱首。

translations.literal: From the move to Ye onward, among the three county magistrates' methods of governance, Qubing alone was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Ye, among the three magistrates' ways of rule, Qubing alone was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，重其能官，與濟陰郡守公孫景茂二人不被替代，發詔褒揚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou pacified Qi, he valued their ability in office—Qubing and Gongsun Jingmao, Administrator of Jiyin, were the two not replaced; an edict was issued to praise and commend them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou conquered Qi, he prized their competence in office. Qubing and Gongsun Jingmao, administrator of Jiyin, were the two not replaced; an edict singled them out for praise.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，卒於冀氏縣令。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, he died while serving as Magistrate of Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era of Sui he died in office as magistrate of Jishi.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses Zhonghua Shuju, November 1972, first edition Book of Northern Qi, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against Zhonghua Shuju, first edition Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
